newsitem.title: QATAR: Gulf Air holds meeting to save indebted airline.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Air holds meeting to save indebted airline.

text.p: Gulf Air shareholders opened an extraordinary meeting in Doha on Wednesday to find ways to improve the $2 billion indebted airline's performance and increase its capital, Qatar's official news agency said.

Bahrain's Transport Ministry Secretary-General for Aviation Affairs Ibrahim al-Hamr told the agency the general assembly aimed at increasing the airline's paid up capital by 100 million Bahraini dinars ($297 million).
Airline officials have put the current capital of the airline -- jointly owned by the governments of Bahrain, Qatar, Oman and Abu Dhabi -- at 150 million Bahraini dinars.
Hamr said the company and its board of directors "were intensifying efforts to improve the company's financial position through a lot of rationalisation measures".

The airline's board of directors had approved a "solid financial plan dealing with a number of rationalisation measures covering the airline's stations, fleet and manpower," he added without elaborating.

The board of directors of the Manama-based airline last met in Muscat in November to study measures to shape up the airline which posted $13 million in profits during the 1996 summer season. It suffered a $159 million loss in 1995.
